The Healthcare Environment and Logistic Management (HELM) Remote Order Entry System (ROES) Supervisor manages the Denver Logistics Center (DLC) and National Acquisition Center (NAC) desktop support, developers, and system administration staff supporting ROES and NAC-Contract Management systems.

The Remote Order Entry System (ROES) is a web-based application and order fulfillment application allowing VHA clinical providers to enter requests for products and services available through the Denver Logistics Center (DLC), and perform other associated functions. ROES is the front end of the DLC's supply chain/order fulfillment system.

ROES is available to VHA and DoD clinical staff in designated disciplines (Audiology & Speech Pathology, Prosthetic & Sensory Aids, Orthotic & Prosthetic Labs, Home Telehealth), who place orders for patient care products and services maintained under DLC contracts.

We are seeking a senior technical leader to spearhead the transformation of our software release and change management practices. In this role, you will transition our traditional, manual change review boards into a modern, automated, and evidence-based governance model.

By embedding security and compliance directly into our automated software pipelines, you will play a central role in ensuring that the technology powering the region is deployed faster, safer, and with unprecedented stability.

As an IT Specialist (Change Authorization & Delivery Lead), you will: Serve as the final authority on system-wide software updates, steering the approval process away from tedious, manual checklist meetings. You will empower teams to focus instead on automated, high-speed validation of code readiness, ensuring every update is justified and safe.

Embed automated security checks, vulnerability scans, and regulatory compliance protocols directly into the software development pipeline. You will shift quality assurance from a final-stage bottleneck into a continuous, automated process that runs seamlessly in the background.

Champion and design low-risk, pre-approved deployment pathways for mature applications. By creating highly automated and reliable pipelines, you will enable teams to rapidly roll out new features and security patches without compromising system stability.

Establish and track modern development metrics-such as deployment frequency, change success rates, and recovery times. You will analyze these data trends to uncover bottlenecks, reduce risks, and make strategic, evidence-based recommendations to executive leadership.

Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate modern project tracking systems (like ServiceNow) directly with automated cloud deployment pipelines (like Azure DevOps). Your goal is to eliminate manual paperwork by automatically generating and filing compliance records as code moves to production.

Design and maintain clear, accessible visual dashboards. These will provide developers, engineers, and executive leaders with instant, real-time insights into upcoming software changes, pipeline health, and overall system performance. Act as the central coordinator and communication hub during major scheduled system updates.

You will align software development and infrastructure teams, ensuring everyone is prepared with robust contingency and rollback plans for a smooth launch. Take the lead during critical outages or software emergencies.

You will coordinate technical teams to deploy emergency patches rapidly, ensuring the system returns to normal operations quickly while still maintaining essential safety controls.

Since launching in May 2024 we've grown to $30 million in ARR. Fyxer is building an AI executive assistant that handles emails, scheduling and follow-up, freeing people in client-facing roles to focus on their customers.
What You'll Be Doing
Own the hardest technical tickets in the business end to end, including the customer conversation, from first report through to resolution
Dogfood Fyxer’s own products, give feedback, and influence our roadmap
Establish blast radius before escalating, because one customer reporting something is a ticket and forty-seven accounts in the same broken state is an incident
Call bug, incident or user error correctly and quickly, and declare it when it's an incident
Write escalations Engineering can act on without a single follow-up question, and stay on them until they land
Spot patterns across Linear and the queue, raising a tracker before the fifth report of something becomes the tenth
Reduce the need for your own role through runbooks, saved queries, Parahelp knowledge, and hands-on upskilling of our senior agents
Here's the honest version of why this role exists. In one recent three-month window we escalated 47 tickets to Engineering and two of them were resolved. Engineering is capacity-constrained, and a third of what we sent them was correctly deprioritised. So this isn't a role that escalates better, it's one that resolves.

You'll be backed by strong Customer Success and Product Engineering teams, and given read-only access to our codebase through Cursor, to our data through our internal tooling, and to our production logs to do it.
What Success Looks Like
You resolve a growing share of technical escalations without Engineering ever being involved
Your escalations are complete, so Engineer can act on them quickly
You use AI and you catch it when it's wrong, before it reaches a customer
You hold a customer's confidence while you investigate, rather than handing them back to someone else
Our senior agents are visibly more capable six months in than they are today, because of you
You're the person the team wants on the ticket because they trust your judgement.

3+ years in a technical support role within a SaaS or cloud-based company
API fluency: you can read an API reference, reason about authentication, and say what a 401 rather than a 500 tells you about where the fault sits
SQL you write yourself: given an unfamiliar schema you work out how the tables relate and write the join unaided
Comfortable in logs, following a request across services and working backwards from an error
Strong written communication, particularly to a customer who is unhappy
Experience with customer support tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, Jira, Linear, others
Startup-ready: adaptable, fast-moving, and hands-on
We're not asking for production engineering experience or a computer science degree. We care what you can do, not how you got there.
Location and other bits
Based in our Chancery Lane office in London, Monday to Thursday, with Fridays from home
Standard office hours
Benefits include: on-site gym, private medical, pension and lunch provided everyday
The Hiring Process
Submit your CV (no need for a cover letter)
We'll review it
An initial call with someone from the hiring team to review your experience and motivation for joining (30 mins)
A call with our Head of Customer Support on your experience and how you think technically (30 minutes)
A live technical exercise (60 minutes)

s.h: Meet more of the team (30 minutes)
s.t: For the exercise we'll give you access to a small example application, a database, an API and its logs, a couple of days ahead, along with three customer tickets. You don't need to solve anything in advance, and you're welcome to use whatever AI tooling you normally would, because that's how the job actually works. We'll be paying attention to how you check its answers.
Our culture is intentional. It stems from the fact we're in the race of our lives to reshape one of the largest AI opportunities that exist; email. There is only first or last.

An obsession around the fact that every second counts, we have to move fast with intensity and drive hard every day.
Never let it slide, be relentless in challenging yourself and others to strive for the best outcome.
This culture is intense; it requires focus and discipline. So we'll do everything we can to remove distraction, support your wellbeing, and reward your impact
